findings.title: Category badge-notification count color not converted for dark theme
findings.body: In `.topic-list.categories .category .badge-notification`, the color rule is still `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%);` and was not wrapped in `dark-light-choose(... , scale-color($secondary, ...))` like every other similar rule in this PR (e.g. the `th`, `td`, `.topic-excerpt`, `.top-date-string` and `div.education` rules a few lines above/below were all converted). As a result, in a dark theme this badge count text will keep using a lightened shade of the (dark) primary color, producing low-contrast/unreadable text against the dark background on the categories topic list, defeating the purpose of this PR for this specific element.

findings.title: Light-mode lightness value changed unintentionally for .topic-meta-data h5 a
findings.body: The original rule was `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. After the change it became `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%));` — the light-mode (first) argument's lightness was changed from 30% to 70%, not just extended with a dark-mode fallback. Every other converted rule in this PR preserves the original lightness for the primary/light-mode branch and uses `100 - lightness` for the secondary/dark branch (e.g. the `.arrow` rule right below correctly keeps 60%/40%). This mismatch changes the rendered color of the embedded-post topic title link in the default (light) theme, which is an unintended visual regression.

findings.title: Light-mode lightness value changed unintentionally for .group-member-info .name
findings.body: Originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`. The PR changed it to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, altering the light-mode lightness from 30% to 50% instead of preserving it (the pattern used everywhere else in this PR keeps the original value as the first argument and uses `100 - value` for the second). The sibling `.title` rule directly below (already 50%/50% before this PR) was left unchanged, suggesting its value was mistakenly duplicated into `.name`. This causes a visible, unintended color change for the member name text in the notifications panel under the default theme.

findings.title: Light-mode lightness value changed unintentionally for .group-member-info .name (mobile)
findings.body: Same issue as the desktop counterpart: originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%);`, now `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`. The light-mode lightness was changed from 30% to 50% rather than being preserved while only adding the dark-theme fallback, producing an unintended color change on mobile for the group member name text in the default theme.

findings.title: Light-mode lightness value swapped for .custom-message-length
findings.body: Originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);`. The converted rule is `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));` — the light-mode and dark-mode lightness values appear swapped: the light-mode branch now uses 30% instead of the original 70%, while 70% was moved to the (wrong) secondary/dark branch. The desktop equivalent in `desktop/modal.scss` correctly keeps 70%/30%. This produces a visibly different (much darker) color for the custom-message-length hint text on mobile in the default theme, and also means the dark-theme fallback does not mirror the original value as intended elsewhere in this PR.

findings.title: Light-mode lightness value changed unintentionally for .topic-map h3 (mobile)
findings.body: Originally `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%);`. The new rule is `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));`, changing the light-mode lightness from 20% to 50%. The desktop equivalent (`desktop/topic-post.scss` `.topic-map h3`) was correctly converted to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, preserving the original 20% value. This mobile/desktop inconsistency confirms the mobile value was altered by mistake, causing an unintended, more muted heading color for the topic-map section header on mobile in the default theme.
